The Jakarta to Bandung high-speed railway, branded Whoosh, opened in October 2023 as the first high-speed line in Southeast Asia. It runs about 140 km from Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia, to Bandung in the hills of West Java, with trains at up to 350 km/h.

Japan and China both bid to build it. In 2015 Indonesia chose China, which offered to build without a government guarantee. It became a flagship of China's Belt and Road Initiative, run by a joint venture of Indonesian and Chinese state companies.

The work ran years late and well over budget, and in the end the government had to put in public money after all. But the line cut the trip between the two cities to under an hour, and President Joko Widodo presented it as proof that Indonesia could build big modern works. Plans call for an extension east toward Surabaya. It joined the Laos to China railway as a sign of how much of the region's new rail was being built by China.
